Subject: EU/APAC deployment constraints — post-call scan & next actions

Hi Claire / Pavlo — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can narrow which Redwood deployment mode fits HelixHealth's constraints.

Recap:
- Primary requirement: Patient PII generated by EU users must remain and be processed within EU jurisdictions (data residency / processing).
- APAC traffic can be handled without strict residency, but low-latency responses for APAC users are preferred.
- HelixHealth wants encryption keys under your control for EU workloads (KMS/HSM integration).
- Procurement is open to a reserved commitment if we can meet residency and SLA targets.

Implication summary:
- Hosted API (hosted.redwood.com): easiest on-boarding but EU residency depends on model and region availability. Not sufficient if keys must be customer-controlled without a Private option.
- Dedicated capacity: provides isolated GPU pool in a cloud region we run for you — can be provisioned in an EU region and supports customer KMS in many cases, but requires an annual/quarterly commit and operational lead time.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): strongest for residency + KMS control; supports air-gapped or customer-managed keys and strict audit controls. More setup and procurement time.

Concrete next steps I propose (please pick owners/ETA):
1) Claire: confirm whether any non-EU telemetry can leave EU (yes/no) and list exactly which data types are considered PII (ETA: Tue 13 Jan).
2) Pavlo: share any preferred EU cloud region (e.g., eu-west-1, europe-west3) and your cloud account ID if you prefer VPC/connect (ETA: Wed 14 Jan).
3) Rishi/Aditya (internal): prepare a short tech note contrasting Dedicated vs Private for HelixHealth (latency, KMS options, timeline, cost ballpark).
4) Kimberly: I will attach a one-page VPC options doc and a SOC2 evidence checklist to help procurement.

If the EU residency requirement for PII is absolute and keys must be customer-held, our Private (VPC) path is likely required; otherwise Dedicated in an EU region could be an acceptable middle ground.

Thanks — I’ll schedule a 30-min follow-up next week for a decision checkpoint.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Kimberly — quick internal note to help the recommendation: 

1) Residency enforcement options:
   - Private VPC (preferred): deploy a customer-dedicated control plane in their cloud account or our Private offering inside a customer VPC. Data never leaves the EU; supports customer KMS and HSM.
   - Dedicated (Redwood-managed in EU): isolated instances in eu-west-1 with customer VPC peering available; data processing stays in EU region, but we manage the infrastructure and keys unless we do a KMS cross-account setup.
   - Hosted: we can pin to EU compute if model and capacity exist, but we cannot guarantee customer-controlled KMS in hosted mode.

2) APAC routing approach:
   - Preferred: serve EU PII in EU (Private/Dedicated) and allow APAC traffic to hit a separate APAC pool (hosted/dedicated). Use a geography-aware gateway in front of Redwood to route by request header or IP.
   - Fallback: if an APAC request includes EU-scoped PII (via user profile or metadata), route to EU pool; otherwise use APAC pool. We need a small header/claim from the app to flag EU-scoped content.

3) Operational notes & timeline:
   - Private VPC: ~6-8 weeks for provisioning + validation (legal + KMS setup + audit).
   - Dedicated EU pool: ~2-3 weeks provisioning, less if capacity exists in eu-west-1.

4) Costs (very rough):
   - Private: higher one-time onboarding + monthly infra pass-through + managed-support premium.
   - Dedicated: mid-level commit pricing (lower unit cost than hosted at high volumes).

I’ll draft a 1-page comparison doc for the customer. Also recommend we propose an interim pilot: stand up a Dedicated EU pool for PII workloads and use Hosted for APAC pilot to accelerate time-to-value while procurement proceeds for Private if needed.

—Rishi
